title: Braid a practice mannequin head's long hair: three sections, six crossings, outer over middle each time, that stay put
instruction: Braid the mannequin head's hair: lay an outer section over the middle one, then the other outer section over the new middle one, and keep alternating sides until there are six crossings. Then let go of the hair.
context: A three-strand braid is the plait people put in their own hair, in a child's before school, or in the hair of someone who cannot do it themselves: carers braid long hair for people in bed or in a wheelchair so it does not tangle, and hairdressing students learn it on a training head like this one. It is done the same way every time: an outer section over the middle one, then the other outer section over the new middle, and repeat. It is hard for a robot because hair is limp and it has two hands for three sections: each section must be pinched near its end, carried over the middle one without dragging the others along, and laid down straight and under light tension on the far side so the crossing forms snug against the last one, and each crossing must stay put while the next is laid. Laid slack, a section bows near the braid, the crossings drift outward and the hair runs out before the sixth; the same side twice only twists two sections together.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A hairdressing training head with long straight synthetic hair (darkest brown, 20 in / 51 cm hair; sold with a table clamp, not used here) lies on its back, face up, on a hand towel folded to about 300 x 250 x 20 mm (centre x 740, y 0), its crown toward the robot at x 590, as for braiding the hair of someone lying in bed. The hair is combed back over the crown onto the bare wooden table and gathered there by one plain hair elastic lying on the table against the crown (x 541-549, y 0). From the elastic the hair is split by eye into three equal sections, each combed smooth and given a light twist so it lies as one round bundle about 10 mm across, 450 mm long; each section's tip is bound by a small elastic 22 mm from its end: red on the section to the robot's right, white on the middle one, blue on the left one. The tip elastics keep each tip together and let a judge tell the sections apart; they take no part in the braid. The sections lie straight on the table in a fan from the elastic: white straight toward the robot to its end at x 100, red 20 degrees to the robot's right to its end near (127, -165), blue 20 degrees to the left to its end near (127, 165). The towel's corners are taped to the table so the head resting in it does not slide; tape marks show the head's crown, the elastic and each section's end. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from a top photo, which may be taken whenever both grippers are at least 3 cm from the hair and no part of the hair moves faster than 1 cm/s (on a real trial, a top-video frame with both hands 3 cm clear where the frame 1 s later shows no section moved 1 cm); the last such photo of the run counts (none: 0). Read the crossings from the gathering elastic outward, tracing each section back from its coloured tip elastic (zoom into the photo or step through the trial video where a crossing is tight): at a crossing the upper section lies over (hides) the lower one. A crossing counts when an outer section lies over the middle one and the sides alternate (right over middle, left over middle, and so on, starting on either side). Counting stops at the first crossing that breaks the pattern: the same side twice in a row, a section passing under the middle one, or a section laid across both others (only its first crossing counts). A section laid over and straight back is no crossing. Score = counted crossings / 6, at most 1.0 (six or more). If the head or the gathering elastic has moved more than 1 cm from its tape marks, the score is 0. The run ends early with success once photos have shown six crossings for 5 seconds in a row.
reset_notes: Unpick the braid. Comb the hair out over the crown and check that the gathering elastic still lies against the crown on its tape mark (re-gather it there if not). Split the hair by eye into three equal sections, comb each smooth, give it a light twist so it lies as one round bundle (synthetic hair left loose spreads flat and frays), and bind its tip again with its own coloured elastic 22 mm from the end (red right, white middle, blue left). Lay the sections straight in the fan, each end on its tape mark, and check the head is on its mark and the towel still taped down. About two minutes.
fidelity: Hair at true length. Each section is one bundle: a chain of 30 rigid 15 mm capsule links with bending springs, stretch and twist locked; single hairs, flyaways, flattening and splitting are not modelled, which is why the real set-up twists each section lightly and binds its tip. Diameter 10 mm, 40 g/m, bending stiffness EI 3e-5 N m^2 and friction 0.8 are estimates. The elastic holds each section's start fixed; the head is fixed. The demo reads the link poses; a model sees only the cameras.
